LIMITATIONS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS ENTRY: (a) this establishes absence IN THE RELEASED ARTEFACT, not that the authors had no rule -- they evidently scored ATE somehow to produce 0.6388, and no cycle may infer from this that their number is wrong, only that its rule is unrecoverable; (b) evaluation/model-prediction.ipynb (15,803 bytes) was NOT READ -- by name and by the README it generates responses rather than scoring them, and there is no cti-ate-responses.tsv for it to have scored, but that is an INFERENCE and reading it is the one cheap unfinished step here; (c) the NeurIPS 2024 camera-ready (proceedings.neurips.cc, or docs/assets/pdfs/ctibench.pdf in the xashru mirror) is the obvious next place to settle Micro-versus-Macro but NO PDF TEXT EXTRACTION IS AVAILABLE to this agent, so neither was read and neither may be cited; (d) the listing is of branch main as of 2026-07-31 with no commit pin.

sources.title: Evaluating Open-Source LLMs for Multi-Label ATT&CK Technique Classification on CTI Reports
key_claims: THIRD INDEPENDENT TEAM IN THIS BASE ON ATT&CK TECHNIQUE MAPPING, AND THE SCORE IS VERY LOW: BEST MICRO-F1 0.22 ON PARENT-LEVEL TECHNIQUES. Authors Ahmed Ryan, Saad Sakib Noor, Md Erfan, Shaswata Mitra, Sudip Mittal, Md Rayhanur Rahman -- no author or institution overlap with CTIBench (src-0002, RIT/Rastogi) or CyberThreat-Eval (src-0007/src-0017, xschen-beb). Verbatim results sentence: 'Across all configurations, the maximum micro F1 score is 0.22, produced by DS236 at (T=0.0, Shot=3, CoT =Yes).' Abstract: 'The highest-performing LLM achieved a micro-averaged F1 score of 0.22'. The seven models (Table I) are DeepSeek-V2.5, GPT-OSS (120B), Llama 3.1 Instruct (70B), Gemma 3 (27B), GPT-OSS (20B), Gemma 3 (12B), Llama 3.1 Instruct (8B). Label granularity is stated verbatim: 'To define a clear boundary for the classification task, we labeled each sentence against the 211 techniques from MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v17.1 (August 2025), omitting the more granular sub-techniques.' Dataset: 'The final dataset comprises 2,076 sentences mapped to 114 unique ATT&CK techniques, totaling 2,028 technique occurrences across 211 potential candidates', from 83 complex unstructured CTI reports (The DFIR Report).

FIRST INTER-ANNOTATOR AGREEMENT STATISTIC IN THIS BASE FOR ATT&CK TECHNIQUE LABELLING. Verbatim: 'Following the six-phase process, we reached a mean inter-annotator agreement of kappa=0.68 across 114 techniques (Landis and Koch: substantial agreement [25]), with 65 techniques (57.0%) exceeding the kappa>=0.7 quality threshold.' Cohen's kappa was 'computed ... per technique to account for chance agreement'. THIS IS AN AGREEMENT STATISTIC, NOT AN ACCURACY BASELINE, AND NOBODY MAY TREAT IT AS DISCHARGING open_questions[1] OUTRIGHT: it does not say how well a human scores against a gold standard, it says two trained humans assigning ATT&CK techniques to the same sentence disagree often enough that 43% of techniques fall below a kappa>=0.7 bar. It is nonetheless the FIRST QUANTITATIVE EVIDENCE IN THIS BASE for the long-asserted and previously unsupported claim that ATT&CK technique assignment is a contested annotation task, and it was measured on PARENT-level techniques, i.e. on the EASIER labelling problem than sub-technique assignment. It is reported as a MEAN over 114 per-technique kappa values with no confidence interval.

SCOPE AND LIMITS, ALL OF WHICH BIND. (a) UNREVIEWED PREPRINT AT v1: arxiv.org/abs/2606.18166 shows submission history '[v1] Tue, 16 Jun 2026 17:04:15 UTC (25 KB)' and carries NO 'Comments:' line and NO 'Journal reference:' line (both checked ABSENT 2026-07-31); Subjects 'Cryptography and Security (cs.CR); Machine Learning (cs.LG)'. (b) THE MODELS ARE OPEN-SOURCE ONLY, SO THIS DOES NOT ANSWER open_questions[0] -- no GPT-5-class, Claude-4.5/Opus-class or Gemini-2.5-class model is evaluated and the 0.22 MUST NOT be read as evidence about 2026-era frontier capability. (c) THE PAPER STATES ITS METRIC BUT NOT ITS ITEM-LEVEL CORRECTNESS RULE: it reports micro-averaged precision, recall and F1 and glosses 'Micro average indicates how well a classifier performs on all the technique instances.', but a verification-mode fetch on 2026-07-31 targeting 'exact match', 'technique ID', 'sub-technique', 'parent technique', 'we count' and 'true positive' found NO sentence stating how a predicted technique is judged correct. Because the label space is declared to be the 211 parent techniques with sub-techniques omitted, the plausible rules collapse toward exact parent-ID set membership -- BUT THAT IS AN INFERENCE AND MUST BE LABELLED AS SUCH, and per rule (v) the ABSENT rests on a single fetch of a single URL form and is NOT a confirmed absence. (d) NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE WITH src-0002's 0.6388 OR src-0007's 0.2787/0.2270: this is sentence-level, parent-level, micro-averaged, on one corpus; those are document-level and (for src-0007) exact-sub-technique-ID. Task format, granularity, corpus and metric aggregation all differ, and ctr-0013 is a standing warning about exactly this move. (e) Single corpus (The DFIR Report), acknowledged by the authors: 'The dataset originates from The DFIR Report and may not generalize to vendor advisories.' and 'Human annotation is subject to interpretive variance'.

APPENDED AT CYCLE 47 BY THE FIRST G2 EVER RUN ON THIS SOURCE. THE kappa=0.68 IS COMPUTED ON A RANDOM 10% SAMPLE OF 195 SENTENCES, AT PHASE (ii) OF SIX, BEFORE RELABELLING AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION. NEITHER RESTRICTION IS RECORDED IN key_claims[1] ABOVE, WHICH STORES THE COMPUTATION CLAUSE TRUNCATED AS 'computed ... per technique to account for chance agreement'. This is ctr-0016, and it answers ctr-0015 step (iv). THE SIX-PHASE PARAGRAPH, PULLED WHOLE AND VERBATIM from https://arxiv.org/html/2606.18166v1 on 2026-08-01 and re-confirmed by a SECOND, SEPARATE exact-string ask on the literal strings 'on a random 10% sample (195 sentences)' and 'which was collected from both annotators', both PRESENT (K written below for the Greek kappa, the only rendering difference): 'We carried out the annotation in six phases: (i) Independent Labeling, where the annotators labeled the allocated reports independently; (ii) Initial Cross-Labeling, where we computed Cohen's Kappa (K) per technique to account for chance agreement on a random 10% sample (195 sentences), which was collected from both annotators; (iii) Relabeling, where the annotators re-evaluated 981 low-agreement sentences (K<0.7), split 460/521 between first and second annotators; (iv) Secondary Cross-Labeling, where we checked 10% of the data relabeled in step-iii (98 sentences) to verify K improvement; (v) Dispute Resolution, where we resolved conflicts via reconciliation meeting; and (vi) Dataset Aggregation, where we merged data of from all phases into the final ground-truth dataset.' THREE CONSEQUENCES. (1) PRECISION: 114 per-technique kappa values estimated from 195 sentences carrying of the order of 200 technique occurrences is of the order of TWO positive instances per technique, and the mean is reported with NO confidence interval. That per-technique occurrence figure is a CYCLE-47 DERIVATION from the printed '2,028 technique occurrences' and '2,076 sentences' and is labelled as such; the printed numbers are exact. (2) A TENSION INSIDE THE SOURCE, NOT A STATE DEFECT, WHICH NOBODY MAY RESOLVE BY PICKING A SIDE: the headline sentence says 'Following the six-phase process, we reached a mean inter-annotator agreement of K=0.68 across 114 techniques (Landis and Koch: substantial agreement), with 65 techniques (57.0%) exceeding the K>=0.7 quality threshold' -- re-verified PRESENT as one whole sentence, so the stored quotation of it is accurate -- yet the paragraph computes kappa at phase (ii), with phase (iv) later described as a re-check 'to verify K improvement'. No sentence read so far states that the 0.68 was recomputed after phase (iv). (3) A NUMBER THIS BASE HAD NEVER RECORDED, AND IT IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN THE 0.68: 981 of 2,076 sentences -- 47.3%, a cycle-47 derivation from two printed numbers -- were 'low-agreement (K<0.7)' and required relabelling. That figure is measured over the WHOLE corpus rather than a sample and is the cleanest quantitative evidence in this base that parent-level ATT&CK sentence labelling is a contested annotation task. WHAT RE-VERIFIED CLEAN AT CYCLE 47: every stored numeral and every other stored quotation in key_claims[0], [1] and [2] returned PRESENT under exact-string ask -- the 0.22 micro-F1 sentence, the full 2,076/114/2,028/211 dataset sentence, the 211-parent-technique granularity sentence, and the DFIR Report caveat; and key_claims[2](a) re-checked clean on 2026-08-01, arxiv.org/abs/2606.18166 still listing '[v1] Tue, 16 Jun 2026 17:04:15 UTC (25 KB)' as its ONLY version with NO 'Comments:' and NO 'Journal reference:' line, so the unreviewed-v1 limit stands. WHAT IS WITHDRAWN: ctr-0015's description of this source's kappa as 'the only one of the three measured over an unrestricted item set' is FALSE and is withdrawn by ctr-0016. All three pooled kappa values are restricted or aggregated, so the '0.68-0.76 band' and 'two teams, two corpora, one conclusion' framings are worse off than ctr-0015 left them and must not be used.

sources.title: TTPrint: Evidence-Grounded TTP Extraction via Diverge-then-Converge Verification
key_claims: FIRST SOURCE IN THIS BASE TO EVALUATE ATT&CK TECHNIQUE MAPPING ON 2026-ERA FRONTIER MODELS, AND IT STATES ITS METRIC AGGREGATION AND ITS LABEL GRANULARITY VERBATIM. Authors Yutong Cheng, Changze Li, Raihan Sultan Pasha Basuki, Qian Cui, Wei Ding, Peng Gao -- independent of CTIBench and of CyberThreat-Eval. Backbones, verbatim: 'GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Open-source models include Qwen 3 235B and DeepSeek v3.2'. METRIC, verbatim from Section 4.1 Evaluation Setup / Metrics: 'TTP extraction is a multi-label prediction problem: each report may map to multiple techniques, and models must identify the complete set. We evaluate at the document level by aggregating predictions across the full report and comparing the resulting technique set to the ground truth. Final scores are macro-averages over all documents: F1bar = 1/|D| sum_{d in D} F1_d'. NOTE CAREFULLY: THIS IS A MACRO AVERAGE OVER DOCUMENTS, NOT OVER CLASSES -- if src-0002's Table 1 header 'Macro-F1' means a macro over TECHNIQUES then the two are DIFFERENT STATISTICS SHARING A NAME, and no cycle may treat them as the same. GRANULARITY, verbatim from the prompt: 'Output only ATT&CK technique IDs in parent-technique format: TXXXX, no child technique like TXXXX.XXX', and from the annotation protocol: 'Annotators labeled at the sentence level: for each sentence, they assigned zero or more parent-level MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs (format: TXXXX)'. The item-level TP/FP/FN algebra is NOT printed -- a targeted fetch for the set-intersection formula returned that the paper 'only references macro-averaged F1 computed per-document without showing the underlying precision/recall calculations'. So the correctness rule is EFFECTIVELY RECOVERABLE (a per-document set comparison over parent-level IDs) BUT AS AN INFERENCE FROM TWO STATED FACTS, NOT AS A QUOTED RULE.

THE EXISTING TRAM BENCHMARK IS DOCUMENTED AS ANNOTATION-NOISY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND TRAINED HUMAN ANNOTATORS AGREE AT kappa 0.74-0.76. Verbatim: 'TRAM contains a significant number of annotation errors, including both false positives and false negatives', categorised by the authors as 'False positives (over-annotation)' and 'False negatives (under-annotation)'. On the new benchmark: 'Each report carries sentence-level annotations produced under double-annotation with adjudication by 3 qualified annotators, achieving Cohen's kappa=0.76'; and 'For TRAM-Clean, we report the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases', at kappa=0.74. Sizes: TRAM-Clean is '2,066 sentences with 665 technique labels across 37 unique techniques'; TTPrint-Bench is 'a new document-level benchmark of 150 CTI reports' that 'covers 125 unique MITRE ATT&CK techniques'. THIS IS THE SECOND INDEPENDENT kappa IN THIS BASE FOR ATT&CK LABELLING AND IT CORROBORATES src-0020's 0.68: trained human annotators on PARENT-level ATT&CK techniques land in the 0.68-0.76 band -- 'substantial' on Landis and Koch, but well short of the near-perfect agreement that an exact-ID scoring rule implicitly presumes. Two independent teams, two corpora, one conclusion.

HEADLINE NUMBERS AND THE CONFOUND THAT GOVERNS THEM. Abstract, verbatim: 'On TRAM-Clean and TTPrint-Bench, TTPrint achieves 76.48% and 87.39% macro-F1 respectively, outperforming the leading baseline by 63.5% and 29.4%.' THESE ARE SYSTEM SCORES FOR TTPrint, NOT BARE-LLM SCORES. TTPrint is a multi-stage scaffold -- divergent decomposition into atomic behaviors, a deterministic span localization stage, then a convergent verification stage that 'retains only candidates supported by both the localized evidence and the authoritative MITRE definition'. COMPARING 76.48/87.39 TO src-0002's 0.6388 OR src-0007's 0.2787 REPRODUCES EXACTLY THE SYSTEM-VERSUS-MODEL CONFOUND THAT ctr-0001 WAS OPENED ABOUT for src-0003's LANCE. A future cycle wanting a model-level comparand must use this paper's per-backbone bare baselines, WHICH WERE NOT CAPTURED AT CYCLE 43 -- capturing the multi-backbone table is the obvious next fetch and is the single highest-value unfinished step on this source. FURTHER LIMITS: (a) AUTHOR-BUILT BENCHMARK, AUTHOR-WINNING RESULT -- TTPrint-Bench was created by the team whose system tops it and TRAM-Clean is their cleaning of someone else's benchmark, and the 'outperforming the leading baseline by 63.5%' figure inherits that; (b) UNREVIEWED PREPRINT AT v1, submission history '[v1] Mon, 25 May 2026 13:31:49 UTC (20,389 KB)', Comments 'Preprint', NO Journal reference, Subjects 'Cryptography and Security (cs.CR); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL)'; (c) NOT COMMENSURABLE OFF THE SHELF WITH src-0020 EITHER despite both being parent-level -- src-0020 is sentence-level micro-F1 over open-source models, this is document-level macro-over-documents F1 over a scaffold, so two parent-level sources is NOT two comparable measurements; (d) authors' own limits: 'TTPrint targets English-language CTI reports' and 'The verification stage relies on the official MITRE ATT&CK ... cannot resolve ambiguity that is structurally present'; (e) NEITHER THIS SOURCE NOR src-0020 SUPPLIES A HUMAN-ANALYST ACCURACY BASELINE (both checked ABSENT), so open_questions[1] is ADVANCED BUT NOT DISCHARGED -- the base now has agreement statistics, not an accuracy baseline.

ADDED CYCLE 46 (T3), DISCHARGING CARRY-FORWARD [80] -- THE PER-BACKBONE AND BARE-LLM BASELINE TABLES, CAPTURED WHOLE. THIS SUPPLIES THE FIRST FRONTIER-MODEL, STATED-GRANULARITY, STATED-AGGREGATION, BARE-MODEL ATT&CK EXTRACTION NUMBER IN THIS ENTIRE BASE. Every cell below was obtained by a discovery fetch of arxiv.org/html/2605.25836v1 and then RE-CONFIRMED by a separate exact-string PRESENT/ABSENT ask per methodological rule (xvii). === TABLE 1, caption verbatim 'Table 1: Document-level results on TRAM-Clean and TTPrint-Bench.' (a trailing 'Best results in bold.' was reported by the discovery fetch but NOT re-confirmed by the exact-string ask, so it is NOT stored as verbatim). Columns in order: Method, Type, then Prec./Rec./F1 for TRAM-Clean, then Prec./Rec./F1 for TTPrint-Bench. ALL FOUR ROWS: TTPDrill, Rule, 1.49, 5.03, 2.19, 4.00, 35.72, 7.16 | One-Shot GPT-4o, LLM, 9.56, 10.51, 9.66, 62.99, 52.80, 44.23 | CoT GPT-4o, LLM, 12.54, 14.59, 12.99, 69.90, 50.70, 58.02 | TTPrint, LLM, 74.59, 82.10, 76.48, 82.15, 95.50, 87.39. The CoT GPT-4o row was re-read cell-by-cell in a second ask and returned identical. THE TWO LLM BASELINE ROWS ARE BARE DIRECT-PROMPTED GPT-4o, NOT SCAFFOLDED, and the paper says so verbatim: 'For LLM-based approaches, we include two direct prompting baselines: One-Shot, which classifies each sentence with one in-context example, and CoT, which adds explicit chain-of-thought reasoning to the same prompt.' A second verbatim anchor on the same numbers: 'One-Shot GPT-4o achieves 52.80% recall and 62.99% precision (F1 44.23%), reflecting incomplete behavior extraction and surface similarity mismatch respectively.' The rule-based comparand is introduced verbatim as 'For rule-based approaches, we include TTPDrill (Husari et al., [2017]), which uses dependency parsing with a manually constructed threat-action ontology and BM25 scoring.' === TABLE 2, 'Effect of LLM backbone on TTPrint-Bench', columns Backbone, Type, Prec., Rec., F1; ALL SIX ROWS: GPT-4o, Closed large, 82.15, 95.50, 87.39 | GPT-4o-mini, Closed small, 61.31, 57.49, 58.01 | Claude Sonnet 4.6, Closed large, 65.09, 80.12, 71.07 | Gemini 2.5 Flash, Closed small, 46.62, 94.41, 61.62 | Qwen 3 235B, Open large, 57.81, 80.91, 66.59 | DeepSeek v3.2, Open large, 67.05, 77.94, 71.04. TABLE 2 IS ENTIRELY SCAFFOLD SCORES -- the full TTPrint pipeline run on six different backbones -- and the paper states this verbatim: 'To test whether TTPrint's gains come from the pipeline architecture rather than a specific LLM, we instantiate the full pipeline with multiple backbones spanning two axes: model family (closed-source vs. open-source) and scale.' and 'All pipeline hyperparameters are held constant across backbones to isolate the effect of the underlying model.' Its GPT-4o row is identical to Table 1's TTPrint TTPrint-Bench cells, which is the internal consistency check one would want. CAUTION RECORDED FOR REUSE: the exact-string ask returned ABSENT for 'Effect of LLM backbone on TTPrint-Bench' while the SAME fetch response quoted 'Table 2: Effect of LLM backbone on TTPrint-Bench' two items later. That ABSENT is SELF-REFUTED WITHIN ONE RESPONSE and is NOT recorded as an absence; per rule (v) no absence is established here. === WHAT THIS LICENSES, AND IT IS THE FIRST CONTROLLED COMPARISON OF ITS KIND IN THIS BASE: within ONE paper, ONE benchmark, ONE metric definition (document-level macro-over-documents F1), ONE label granularity (parent-level TXXXX) and ONE backbone (GPT-4o), the progression is bare One-Shot 44.23 -> bare CoT 58.02 -> full TTPrint scaffold 87.39 on TTPrint-Bench, and 9.66 -> 12.99 -> 76.48 on TRAM-Clean. NOTHING IN THIS BASE PREVIOUSLY HELD A BARE-VERSUS-SCAFFOLD PAIR SCORED UNDER ONE RULE. === ONE FURTHER FINDING ABOUT THE ABSTRACT'S HEADLINE DELTA, AND IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE ABSTRACT INVITES THE WRONG READING. The abstract's 'outperforming the leading baseline by 63.5% and 29.4%' is an ABSOLUTE PERCENTAGE-POINT DIFFERENCE, NOT A RELATIVE IMPROVEMENT. The body states it verbatim with the arithmetic shown: 'CoT GPT-4o at 58.02%) and 76.48% on TRAM-Clean (+63.49 over CoT GPT-4o at 12.99%).' Cycle 46's own arithmetic check, LABELLED AS DERIVED BY THIS CYCLE per rule (xii) and not as a source statement: 76.48 minus 12.99 = 63.49, matching the abstract's 63.5; and 87.39 minus 58.02 = 29.37, matching the abstract's 29.4. The RELATIVE reading would give 76.48/12.99 = 5.9x, i.e. roughly +489%, so misreading the '%' sign as relative would be a large error. It also identifies the 'leading baseline' as CoT GPT-4o specifically. NOTE THAT THE ABLATION FIGURES USE THE SAME PERCENTAGE-POINT CONVENTION: 'Removing verification causes the largest precision drop (delta=-26.6%, from 82.15% to 55.55%) and the largest overall F1 degradation (delta=-23.0%), as all proposed candidates are accepted without evidence-based scrutiny.' -- and 82.15 minus 55.55 = 26.60 confirms it.

ADDED CYCLE 46 (T3) AS THE RESULT OF THIS SOURCE'S FIRST G2. VERSION AND VENUE RE-CHECKED, AND TWO QUOTATION DEFECTS FOUND IN THIS BASE'S OWN ACCOUNT OF THE SOURCE -- SEE ctr-0015. VERSION STALENESS CHECK (bolt-on, arXiv sources): re-fetched arxiv.org/abs/2605.25836 on 2026-08-01. The submission history still lists '[v1] Mon, 25 May 2026 13:31:49 UTC (20,389 KB)' AND NO LATER VERSION; 'Comments: Preprint' is still PRESENT; there is still NO 'Journal reference:' line; Subjects still 'Cryptography and Security (cs.CR); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL)'; DOI is the arXiv-minted https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2605.25836, i.e. NOT a publisher DOI. SO THE 'UNREVIEWED v1 PREPRINT' LIMIT IN claim 2(b) IS RE-CONFIRMED AS OF 2026-08-01 AND HAS NOT GONE STALE. SIXTEEN STORED QUOTATIONS WERE EXACT-STRING CHECKED AGAINST arxiv.org/html/2605.25836v1 AND ALL SIXTEEN RETURNED PRESENT, with the document confirmed complete through its References section (so no rule-(xvi) truncation hazard applies to this render). TWO DEFECTS WERE NONETHELESS FOUND, BOTH IN HOW THE QUOTATIONS WERE STORED RATHER THAN IN THE SOURCE -- the rule-(vi) shape, a clean source with a defective account of it. DEFECT 1, A SPLICE: claim 0 stores the backbone list as the single quoted run 'GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Open-source models include Qwen 3 235B and DeepSeek v3.2'. The source has TWO sentences and the first one BEGINS 'Closed-source models include GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash.' The stored run drops the leading clause 'Closed-source models include' with no ellipsis while retaining the parallel clause of the following sentence, so it reads as one continuous sentence that does not exist. The MODEL LIST ITSELF IS CORRECT AND COMPLETE and no downstream claim changes; the correct verbatim pair is now stored here. DEFECT 2, AN OMITTED PARENTHETICAL THAT RESCOPES A NUMBER, AND THIS ONE IS SUBSTANTIVE: claim 1 stores 'For TRAM-Clean, we report the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases' and stops there. THE SOURCE SENTENCE CONTINUES: 'For TRAM-Clean, we report the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases (i.e., cases that reached the adjudication stage).' The omitted parenthetical is the definition of 'contested cases' and it establishes that the kappa=0.74 figure is computed over an ADJUDICATION-SELECTED HARD SUBSET, not over all annotations. This is the ctr-0012 shape exactly -- a subordinate clause of the very sentence this base quotes, dropped in the storing. CONSEQUENCE: the 0.74 is NOT the same statistic as this paper's own 0.76 (all annotations on TTPrint-Bench) and NOT the same statistic as src-0020's 0.68 (a mean over 114 per-technique kappas), so the '0.68-0.76 band' framing in claim 1 and in ttp-attack-mapping-reliability open_questions[1] OVER-POOLS THREE DIFFERENT STATISTICS. ctr-0015 is opened on this. Note also, as pure rendering rather than defect, that the source prints the Greek letter kappa where this base stores the word 'kappa'.

sources.title: The end of the curl bug-bounty
key_claims: PRIMARY-SOURCE ACCOUNT OF THE curl/HackerOne CLOSURE, THE SOURCE EIGHT SUCCESSIVE CYCLES NAMED AS THE MOST VALUABLE UNCOLLECTED ITEM IN THIS PROJECT AND WHICH G1 FORBADE ANYONE INVENTING. Daniel Stenberg, curl's lead maintainer, posting 26 January 2026. Verbatim: 'There is no longer a curl bug-bounty program. It officially stops on January 31, 2026.' Replacement process, verbatim: 'If you suspect a security problem in curl going forward, we advise you to head over to GitHub and submit them there.' Programme scale to date, verbatim: '87 confirmed vulnerabilities and over 100,000 USD paid as rewards to researchers.' This is a documented real-world case of AI-generated security reporting degrading a triage pipeline to the point of programme closure -- reliability failure measured not by a benchmark but by an institution abandoning a process. It serves automated-triage-under-refusal and institutional-incident-real-world-impact.

THE QUANTITATIVE CORE: THE CONFIRMED-VALID RATE FELL BELOW 5%. Verbatim: 'Starting 2025, the confirmed-rate plummeted to below 5%. Not even one in twenty was real.' (the emphasis on 'real' is the author's). FEWER THAN ONE IN TWENTY SUBMISSIONS TO A MAJOR OPEN-SOURCE BOUNTY PROGRAMME WAS A REAL VULNERABILITY FROM 2025 ONWARD. CRITICAL SCOPE LIMIT: THIS IS NOT AN AI-ATTRIBUTABLE ERROR RATE. It is the overall confirmed rate of an inbound stream containing AI-generated, AI-assisted and purely human reports, and it is NOT decomposed by whether a given report was AI-generated. Using it as a proxy for AI-generated report validity would be an over-attribution that the source's own three-trends sentence contradicts. There is also NO before/after control: no pre-2025 confirmed-rate figure is captured, so 'plummeted' is the author's characterisation and this base has no baseline number anchoring the size of the fall.

THE STATED CAUSE IS THREE COMBINED TRENDS, NOT AI ALONE, AND THIS IS THE THING A SUCCESSOR IS MOST LIKELY TO GET WRONG. Verbatim: 'There are these three bad trends combined that makes us take this step: the mind-numbing AI slop, humans doing worse than ever and the apparent will to poke holes rather than to help.' ANY CLAIM IN THIS STATE THAT READS 'curl closed its bounty because of AI' IS AN OVER-ATTRIBUTION AND MUST BE SCOPED TO THAT SENTENCE. On contamination beyond the obvious cases, verbatim: 'We saw an explosion in AI slop reports combined with a lower quality even in the reports that were not obvious slop - presumably because they too were actually misled by AI but with that fact just hidden better.' THAT SECOND SENTENCE'S CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION IS HEDGED BY THE AUTHOR HIMSELF ('presumably', 'just hidden better') AND MUST BE CARRIED WITH ITS HEDGE INTACT -- ctr-0012 exists in this base purely because a hedging subordinate clause was dropped in every downstream rendering of a quoted sentence. CHECKED AND ABSENT FROM THE POST, single fetch and one URL form so NOT confirmed absences under rule (v): (a) NO percentage of reports stated to be AI-generated -- secondary coverage attributes a '~20% of all reports are AI-generated' figure to Stenberg, and THAT FIGURE IS NOT IN THIS POST, WAS NOT COLLECTED, AND MUST NOT BE ENTERED INTO THIS STATE FROM A SEARCH SNIPPET; (b) NO count of reports received in a specific January 2026 window -- secondary coverage cites 'seven reports in 16 hours' and 'more than 20 by mid-month, none real', under the same prohibition. FURTHER LIMITS: personal blog post by an interested party, not peer reviewed, no external audit -- Stenberg is the maintainer whose time was consumed and is describing his own decision, and the 'below 5%' and '87 / 100,000 USD' figures are his report of his own programme's records, not independently verifiable from this source; N=1 institution and an unusually high-profile, unusually thin-staffed one, so nothing here generalises to bounty programmes at large and nothing here measures any specific LLM. The related primary artefact https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/20312 ('BUG-BOUNTY.md: we stop the bug-bounty end of Jan 2026 by bagder') was seen in search results but WAS NOT FETCHED and is not cited.

[CORRECTION APPENDED AT CYCLE 59, DISCHARGING ctr-0018 STEPS (i) AND (ii). THAT SENTENCE IS FALSE AND ctr-0018 (cycle 50) established why at source. The post DOES state a pre-2025 baseline. The FULL PARAGRAPH, verbatim and in order, is: 'Maybe the first five years made it possible for researchers to find and report the low hanging fruit. Previous years we have had a rate of somewhere north of 15% of the submissions ending up confirmed vulnerabilities. Starting 2025, the confirmed-rate plummeted to below 5%. Not even one in twenty was real.' Cycle 43 quoted the third and fourth sentences and missed the SECOND. THE BASELINE SENTENCE IS THEREFORE: 'Previous years we have had a rate of somewhere north of 15% of the submissions ending up confirmed vulnerabilities.' It was confirmed on a SECOND URL FORM -- the monthly archive listing https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2026/01/ , which serves the post body in full and independently returned PRESENT for the exact string 'north of 15%' with the identical sentence. FOUR CAVEATS TRAVEL WITH THE 15% FIGURE AND ARE NOT OPTIONAL, being exactly those already attached to 'below 5%': (1) it is the maintainer's report of his own programme's records, self-reported and not externally audited, with no stated methodology; (2) 'somewhere north of' is explicitly approximate by the author's own wording and is NOT a point estimate; (3) no year is attached to 'previous years', so the baseline WINDOW IS UNDEFINED and no rate-of-change per year may be derived from it; (4) like 'below 5%', it is an OVERALL confirmed-valid rate over a mixed inbound stream and is NOT decomposed by whether a report was AI-generated, so the pair does NOT measure an AI-attributable error rate. sources.title: CTIArena (v1) / CTIConnect (v2): A Benchmark for LLMs over Heterogeneous Cyber Threat Intelligence
key_claims: A PEER-REVIEWED CTI BENCHMARK WITH A DEDICATED ATTRIBUTION TASK FAMILY THAT MEASURES NO CONFIDENCE CONSTRUCT OF ANY KIND. Collected at cycle 49 to test the primary open question of attribution-expressed-confidence-unmeasured. Two fetches on two URL forms -- which served TWO DIFFERENT VERSIONS of the paper -- each instructed to answer PRESENT/ABSENT and to write ABSENT rather than infer, returned ABSENT for every confidence construct. The unversioned /html render (= v2) was asked as an exact-string sweep over the ENTIRE document including appendices and prompt templates and returned ABSENT for ALL of: 'calibration', 'Expected Calibration Error', 'ECE', 'Brier', 'confidence', 'likelihood', 'abstain', 'abstention', 'I don't know', 'insufficient evidence', 'uncertain', 'logprob', 'how certain'. The only PRESENT was 'probability', in a sentence about the LLM judge rather than an elicited confidence. The v1 render returned ABSENT for calibration statistics, for any request that the model state a confidence/probability/likelihood/certainty, for abstention or refusal measurement, and for hedging or token-level probabilities. CONCLUSION, PROPERLY SCOPED: this benchmark scores its attribution-family tasks by CORRECTNESS ONLY, and it joins src-0002 and src-0007 as a THIRD CTI benchmark with an attribution task that does not measure expressed confidence on it.

PROVENANCE, AND IT IS UNUSUAL: THE PAPER CHANGED ITS NAME AND ITS CONTENT BETWEEN VERSIONS, SO THIS ARXIV ID MUST NOT BE CITED BY A SINGLE TITLE. The /abs page on 2026-08-01 gives title 'CTIConnect: A Benchmark for Retrieval-Augmented LLMs over Heterogeneous Cyber Threat Intelligence'; authors Yutong Cheng, Yang Liu, Changze Li, Dawn Song, Peng Gao; submission history verbatim '[v1] Monday, 13 October 2025, 22:10:17 UTC (667 KB)' and '[v2] Wednesday, 3 June 2026, 17:07:57 UTC (3,226 KB)'; Subjects 'Cryptography and Security (cs.CR); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)'; Comments 'Accepted to KDD 2026'; Journal reference ABSENT; only DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2510.11974. But arxiv.org/html/2510.11974v1 returns a paper titled CTIArena with a DIFFERENT task list. So the work is PEER-REVIEWED AND ACCEPTED at KDD 2026 (contrast src-0005 and src-0015, both unreviewed preprints), and it was renamed and substantially rewritten between v1 and v2 -- a live instance of methodological rule (v)'s fourth check, that the VERSION fetched must contain the material at all. v1 task list (from a DISCOVERY fetch, so a summary and NOT verbatim): RCM, WIM, ATD, ESD, ATA and VCA scored by exact string matching with regex normalisation, and CSC, Threat Actor Profiling (TAP) and MLA scored by an LLM judge against a structured rubric reported as F1. v2 abstract VERBATIM: 'We construct a unified evaluation environment integrating five heterogeneous CTI sources into 1,860 expert-verified QA pairs spanning nine tasks across three categories: Entity Linking, Multi-Document Synthesis, and Entity Attribution.' An attribution-family task is present in BOTH versions.

LIMITS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS ENTRY. (a) APPENDIX D WAS NOT READABLE IN EITHER FETCH: the v1 fetch reported TRUNCATED, cutting off mid-sentence inside the Appendix D prompt templates, and the v2 fetch reported it could NOT see Appendix D at all, naming 'A.4. Magniber Cross-Source Correlation Case Study' as the last visible heading while confirming the References WERE visible. PROMPT TEMPLATES ARE EXACTLY WHERE AN INSTRUCTION TO STATE A CONFIDENCE LEVEL WOULD LIVE, so under methodological rule (xvi) the absence above is established for the readable BODY of two versions and is NOT established for the prompt templates; the ar5iv render or the KDD 2026 proceedings is the way to close it. (b) THE TWO FETCHES DISAGREE ON THE JUDGE MODEL -- the v1 render returned a truncated 'we employ GPT-5 as an automatic judge guided by a structured rubric...' and the v2 render returned 'we employ GPT-4 as an automatic judge guided by a structured rubric.' -- and under rule (xvii) neither is storable, so THIS BASE RECORDS NO CLAIM ABOUT WHICH MODEL JUDGES THIS BENCHMARK. It is plausibly just the version difference, but that was not confirmed and is not asserted in either direction. (c) NO PER-MODEL NUMBER IS RECORDED because none was verified; nothing here may be used to rank models or to state an attribution accuracy.

SCOPE NOTE ON WHAT THIS SOURCE DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE FOR attribution-expressed-confidence-unmeasured. It is EVIDENCE FOR A NEGATIVE and is entered as such. It does NOT show that expressed confidence on attribution is unmeasurable, nor that models are or are not overconfident when attributing; it shows that one more peer-reviewed CTI benchmark with an attribution task chose not to measure it. Per that issue's own exclusion rule, this source's correctness scores do NOT count as a confidence measurement at any exchange rate.

[CYCLE-59 G2 RE-VERIFICATION -- THE FIRST INDEPENDENT CHECK THIS SOURCE HAS EVER HAD. MIXED. ctr-0024 OPENED. APPENDED, NOT SUBSTITUTED.] Chosen because src-0023 was the LAST source in this base with no G2 behind it; carry-forward [109] is now FULLY DISCHARGED. TWO NEW URL FORMS, neither used by any prior cycle: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2510.11974 (serves v1, titled CTIArena) and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11974v2 (serves v2, titled CTIConnect). Both fetched in verification mode with an item-0 body probe, a final truncation probe, and 'do NOT substitute a nearby or similar sentence'. WHAT HOLDS: key_claims[0]'s CONCLUSION -- that this benchmark measures no elicited confidence construct -- survives on both new renders. 'calibration' ABSENT on both. 'abstain'/'abstention' ABSENT on ar5iv/v1. No prompt-template instruction to state a confidence, probability, certainty or likelihood on either. WHAT FAILS, AND IT IS A LITERAL FALSIFICATION OF A STORED EXACT-STRING ABSENT: key_claims[0] asserts the v2 render was swept for exact strings over the ENTIRE document and returned ABSENT for 'confidence'. The explicit-v2 render returns PRESENT, quoting verbatim 'LLM-based judge (GPT-4) filters low-confidence samples via a structured rubric'. The string 'confidence' IS in v2, inside 'low-confidence'. Cycle 49's sweep verdict was wrong on that string. It does NOT overturn the conclusion, because the occurrence concerns FILTERING BENCHMARK-CONSTRUCTION DATA by judge score, not eliciting a confidence from an evaluated model -- exactly the distinction cycle 49 itself drew for 'probability'. See ctr-0024. THE JUDGE-MODEL DISCREPANCY IS NOW EXPLAINED AND HALF-CLOSED, per cycle 58's refinement of rule (ix). Asked for the WHOLE PARAGRAPH, the explicit-v2 render returned verbatim: 'For multi-document synthesis tasks, we use GPT-4 as an automatic judge guided by a structured rubric. The judge is comprehensively validated on a 20% expert-annotated sample, achieving Cohen's kappa=0.85 with three CTI experts (inter-human kappa=0.93), 93.9% self-consistency over five runs, and a stylistic-bias differential of only 0.013 between GPT-family and non-GPT outputs (full protocol and results in Section A.1).' (the page prints the Greek letter kappa; 'kappa' above stands for it). That is GPT-4 confirmed on a SECOND, distinct URL form of v2, and https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11974 -- the URL this source actually cites -- serves v2. THIS BASE MAY THEREFORE NOW STATE: IN v2 (CTIConnect) THE MULTI-DOCUMENT-SYNTHESIS JUDGE IS GPT-4. The v1 'GPT-5' reading is neither refuted nor resolved: it came from a truncated v1 render, and the ar5iv v1 render returns ABSENT for the exact string 'automatic judge' altogether, reporting 'LLM judge' and 'LLM-based judge' instead. v1's judge model remains UNSTORABLE, and v1 is a DIFFERENT DOCUMENT from the one the /abs URL serves. NEW FACT, ANSWERING THE QUESTION CYCLE 50 FLAGGED AND WHICH NO CYCLE CHECKED IN THE NINE SINCE -- does this benchmark report an ATT&CK/TTP mapping task, and under what scoring rule: YES, in BOTH versions, and the scoring rule is now verbatim. v2: 'CTI-ATA (Attack Technique Attribution, Report to ATT&CK entries) identifies all MITRE ATT&CK techniques described in a threat report passage', scored by 'Precision, Recall, and F1-score after regex-based identifier normalization'. v1/ar5iv: 'This task identifies attack behaviors in narrative reports that can be mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques', the task named 'Closed-Book Attack Technique Attribution (ATA)'. This is directly relevant to ttp-attack-mapping-reliability, which no cycle has yet wired it into. NO PER-MODEL SCORE IS RECORDED because none was verified, so nothing here states how well any model performs CTI-ATA. ALSO NEW: v1's size is 'The final benchmark comprises 691 QA pairs: 371 structured, 150 unstructured, and 170 hybrid', against v2's stored 1,860 -- consistent with the recorded rewrite, NOT a conflict. APPENDIX D REMAINS UNREAD AFTER A THIRD AND FOURTH FETCH, so key_claims[2](a)'s limit STANDS. The explicit-v2 render reported NO Appendix D visible, naming 'A.4. Magniber Cross-Source Correlation Case Study' as its last heading and listing only A through A.4 -- IDENTICAL to cycle 49's v2 result, so v2 appears to have no Appendix D at all and the label may be a v1-only artefact. The ar5iv/v1 render claimed to see 'Appendix D Prompt Template' and appendices A-E, but the SAME fetch reported itself TRUNCATED mid-body inside the ATA task description, so under rule (xvi) its appendix listing is unusable and its ABSENT about prompt-template confidence instructions carries no weight. ar5iv ALSO returned a rule (xvii) defect: asked for the exact string 'confidence' it answered PRESENT and quoted a sentence not containing the word, so ar5iv's 'confidence' verdict is DISCARDED and only the explicit-v2 hit is relied on above.

sources.title: Expressing confidence/estimative probability in an analysis (MISP best-practices-in-threat-intelligence)
key_claims: THE OPERATIONAL CTI STANDARD FOR EXPRESSING CONFIDENCE SEPARATES THREE DISTINCT AXES, AND THE SEPARATION IS THE POINT. This is a normative best-practice document for HUMAN analysts containing no LLM, no model, no number and no experiment; it is entered ONLY to answer the DESIGN question in attribution-expressed-confidence-unmeasured open_questions[3]. Verbatim: 'Expressing the confidence or the lack of it in an analysis is a critical step to help a partner or a third-party to check your hypotheses and conclusions.' and 'Analysis or reports are often shared together with technical details, but often lack the associated overall confidence level.' It names two MISP taxonomies, admiralty-scale and estimative-language, and gives verbatim tag examples 'admiralty-scale:source-reliability="a/b/c..."', 'estimative-language:likelihood-probability="almost-no-chance"' and 'estimative-language:confidence-in-analytic-judgment="moderate"'. These are NOT three interchangeable ways of saying 'how sure am I': source-reliability grades the SOURCE, likelihood-probability grades how likely the claim is to be TRUE (Kent-style words of estimative probability), and confidence-in-analytic-judgment grades confidence in the JUDGMENT ITSELF, i.e. in the sufficiency of the evidence and reasoning behind it. Axes 2 and 3 are separately tagged and can move independently.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN QUESTION: THE MEASUREMENT attribution-expressed-confidence-unmeasured ASKS FOR ALREADY EXISTS AS A STANDARDISED, MACHINE-READABLE CONSTRUCT -- IT IS SIMPLY NOT APPLIED TO LLMs BY ANYTHING FOUND SO FAR. That issue reasoned independently, from the other direction, that the well-posed target is not 'is the model calibrated' but whether a model's expressed confidence DISCRIMINATES between reports whose attribution is determined by the evidence and reports whose attribution is not. 'confidence-in-analytic-judgment' IS that quantity under an operational name, and the standard already distinguishes it from likelihood. The document also states the practical purpose of machine-readable confidence tagging, verbatim: 'Allow receiving organisations to filter, classify and score the information in an automated way based on related tags'. So the design objection that attribution confidence is too ill-posed to measure because attribution ground truth is contested does NOT hold: operational practice resolves it by splitting the probability judgement from the evidential-sufficiency judgement.

LIMITS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS ENTRY. (a) IT IS A NORMATIVE STANDARD, NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT MODEL BEHAVIOUR, and can never be cited as a measurement of any LLM. (b) It is a community best-practice repository file, not peer-reviewed: no DOI, no venue, no stated author, and it was read from branch master with NO COMMIT PIN, so a successor should re-pin it. (c) THE LEVEL SETS THEMSELVES WERE NOT READ -- the file gives only EXAMPLE tag values ('a/b/c...', 'almost-no-chance', 'moderate'), and the full enumerations live on the linked MISP taxonomy pages (misp-project.org/taxonomies.html#_admiralty_scale and #_estimative_language), which cycle 49 did NOT fetch; nobody may state how many levels each axis has without fetching them. (d) The exact string 'JP 2-0' is ABSENT from this file (checked): a web-search summary attributed a JP 2-0 reference to this document and that attribution is WRONG, recorded here so nobody re-imports it. (e) The Admiralty scale's information-credibility axis (the numeric half that normally accompanies the A-F source-reliability half) is NOT named in this file; only source-reliability appears, and its presence must not be assumed.

CYCLE 58 G2 -- THE FIRST INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION THIS SOURCE HAS EVER RECEIVED, AND THE FIRST PERFORMED ON EITHER OF THE TWO SOURCES CYCLE 49 ADDED (see carry-forward [109]). VERDICT: PASSED CLEAN ON BOTH URL FORMS, AND THE VERSION IS NOW PINNED. PER RULE (v), ALL THREE OF THIS ENTRY'S ABSENT VERDICTS WERE RE-ASKED ON A SECOND URL FORM -- https://github.com/MISP/best-practices-in-threat-intelligence/blob/master/best-practices/expressing-confidence.adoc -- AND ALL THREE CONFIRMED ABSENT: 'JP 2-0' (limit (d)), any string containing 'credibility' (limit (e)), and any mention of an LLM, language model, AI, machine learning or experimental number (limit (a)). Limit (c) is re-confirmed on both forms: asked directly whether the file contains any full enumeration of either taxonomy's levels rather than one or two examples, both answered NO. RULE (xx) CHECK, RUN SPECIFICALLY BECAUSE state/knowledge/src-0024.md CLAIMS TO REPRODUCE 'the whole file, verbatim' AND A DEFINITE ARTICLE IS EXACTLY WHAT RULE (xx) SAYS TO RE-ENUMERATE: the second form was asked to reproduce the file from its very first line to its very last, including any AsciiDoc headers, attributes, anchors, includes or bibliography entries; it reported 24 lines in total, answered NOT TRUNCATED, and answered NO both to whether any text precedes the heading line and to whether any text follows the threat-intelligence.eu sentence. THE DEFINITE ARTICLE SURVIVES -- the stored reproduction is complete, and this is the first instance in this project where a rule (xx) re-enumeration has CONFIRMED rather than refuted the state's account (contrast ctr-0023). VERSION PIN, WHICH DISCHARGES THE FIRST HALF OF LIMIT (b): api.github.com/repos/MISP/best-practices-in-threat-intelligence/commits?path=best-practices/expressing-confidence.adoc returns FIVE commits, unpaginated, the most recent being sha dbc27c3b5faeae50ecec94798255242c3c8aefcb dated 2022-11-06T16:20:32Z with message 'chg: [clean-up] various updates and some refs to new features', and the earliest dated 2018-09-22T19:21:41Z. THE FILE HAS NOT CHANGED SINCE NOVEMBER 2022, so it predates every cycle of this project by more than three years and carries NO version-staleness risk; a successor wanting a pinned render may use raw.githubusercontent.com/MISP/best-practices-in-threat-intelligence/dbc27c3b5faeae50ecec94798255242c3c8aefcb/best-practices/expressing-confidence.adoc.
